verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Ubuntu can replace Windows or dual-boot from a bootable USB. They also cite support for older hardware, Raspberry Pi/Arm certification and devices from Dell, HP and Lenovo, plus documented NVIDIA driver installation and DKMS module building. One community comment notes that NVIDIA hardware needs proprietary driver blobs, which is a caveat rather than a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of freedom from vendor lock-in (open licensing, no account or vendor tie-in), a published hardware compatibility scope beyond the named OEMs, and independent or hands-on confirmation of installs on arbitrary hardware.
